name: tera_render
description: Render a Tera template, optionally with a JSON context. Supports the full Tera vocabulary: variables, filters, conditionals, for loops, autoescape, and inclusion. Options are keyword-only named parameters with defaults — `autoescape := false` for non-HTML output, `template_path := './templates/*.html'` to load templates from disk by name. They must be constant expressions; unknown option names or values of the wrong type are rejected when the query is bound, and a NULL argument (including a NULL option) makes the result NULL.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Template source, or a template name when `template_path` is set.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: JSON context the template is rendered against — a literal, a JSON column, or `json_object(...)` built from columns. Omit it for templates without variables.

parameters.name: autoescape
parameters.description: HTML-escape interpolated values (`B&O` becomes `B&O`), in inline templates and in `template_path` files whatever their extension. Pass `false` for plain text, configs, SQL or JSON output.

parameters.name: template_path
parameters.description: Glob of template files to load (for example `'./templates/*.html'`). When set, `template` is a template name, which enables `{% extends %}` / `{% include %}` / `{% import %}`. Empty means inline templates only.

parameters.name: autoescape_extensions
parameters.description: Only used with `template_path`: when non-empty, file templates are HTML-escaped only if their name ends with one of these suffixes (for example `['.html']`). With the default `[]`, `autoescape` applies to every template. Has no effect when `autoescape` is false. Inline templates follow `autoescape` and ignore this list. Must not contain NULL elements.
